openings.claim: Stale exception locations contribute to delayed correct-hold retrieval; fixing location consistency may reduce second searches. The supplied synthetic observations establish neither causation nor improvement.
openings.delta: After checking the paper exception slip, keep listed holds at their recorded addresses throughout the evening. Newly arrived books remain on the existing cart for that window instead of moving during service.
openings.prediction: With location drift prevented, second-location searches and retrieval time fall, including during equally busy intervals.
openings.rival_prediction: Household-name misfiling is the main search problem: stable exception addresses leave delays concentrated among books filed under another household member.
openings.defeat: Verified stable exception locations produce unchanged second-search frequency, while delayed encounters consistently involve household-name mismatches.
openings.probe: Propose a bounded evening trial: reconcile exceptions within a ten-minute total preparation-and-correction budget, freeze their locations, and time retrieval using the existing sheet. Keep names behind the desk and reader verification at clerk handoff. Record discrepancies and cart crowding. If reconciliation exceeds the budget, reject feasibility; do not relax it. Evaluate this probe separately from an unproven full rollout.
assumptions: The clerk can verify hold ownership using existing information.
Cart capacity may be insufficient at larger arrival volumes.
The full reconciliation may not fit ten minutes.

openings.claim: How much of the two-minute failure is waiting for the sole clerk rather than searching?
openings.delta: Separate arrival-to-service waiting from service-to-correct-handoff time before choosing a throughput intervention.
openings.prediction: If clerk congestion dominates, excess duration clusters in the 25-minute peak even for direct, correct retrievals.
openings.rival_prediction: Location errors dominate: excess duration follows second searches outside and inside the peak, with little waiting contribution.
openings.defeat: Measured waiting contributes negligibly to delayed encounters.
openings.probe: Use anonymous encounter numbers on the existing timing sheet to record arrival, service start, and handoff during a proposed evening sample; include setup in the ten-minute budget. Compare direct retrievals and second searches within and outside the peak.
assumptions: The clerk can record timestamps without materially delaying handoffs.
The success measure includes waiting from reader arrival.
